what_happened: The job "Version scoring rules so old scores verify; gate rule changes on history" (20261017-114155-ksq0) ended failed at admission, before any work was done. Admission refused it because .github/workflows/ci.yml is a governance file. A job may change that file only if the accepted reading lists it as a deliverable and names it in an acceptance criterion. This reading did not. The event lists no unmet acceptance criteria, blocker or major findings, or failed checks. Nothing was delivered.
cause: Gating rule changes on history is a CI concern, so the outcome naturally needs a workflow edit. The step that turns a request into a reading does not work out which files the outcome will touch, and it does not compare them with the governance-protected list. That list is enforced only at admission, after the reading is accepted and the job submitted. A gap in the reading therefore shows up as a refused job, not as a correction made while the reading is drafted. The same gap already refused an athena.toml job a few hours earlier, and nothing carried that lesson forward.
prevention: Add a check at the reading stage, before acceptance. It would take the files the reading's deliverables are expected to touch, using the request's keywords such as CI, gate, workflow and config plus a scan of the repo. It would compare them with the governance-protected list. For every protected file that is hit, the check would require the reading to list it as a deliverable and name it in an acceptance criterion. If it does not, the reading is rejected or auto-amended. The same check should run on submit, so a job is never queued that admission will refuse.
proposed_request: Version the scoring rules so that scores produced under an old rule version still verify under the rules that were in force when they were made. Also gate changes to scoring rules on history: a rule change must be checked against past recorded scores, and must fail if any previously verifying score would stop verifying. Deliverables: the versioned scoring rules and their verification code; the history-based gate check; and the change to .github/workflows/ci.yml that runs this gate in CI. The workflow file is a governance file, so it is an explicit deliverable. Acceptance criteria: (1) .github/workflows/ci.yml is changed and runs the history gate on pull requests; (2) a score recorded under an old rule version verifies after a new version is added; (3) a rule change that would break an old score makes the gate fail, shown by a test; (4) existing checks still pass.
